summary: A 1934 L-4 lookout on this cliff-top site was replaced in 1964 by a helicopter-placed R-6 groundhouse, one of only two surviving lookouts on the Tiller Ranger District.

staffing.status: nominally still used for fire detection, largely superseded by aerial surveillance

access.note: High-clearance 4WD/AWD vehicle to trailhead, then a moderately steep 0.4-mile hike in; not rented in winter due to wind/snow load.

visit.trail_note: 0.4-mile forested trail from the trailhead to the lookout.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: First lookout on the site, an L-4 cab.
L-4 replaced by the present R-6 flat-roofed groundhouse, reportedly placed by helicopter.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, September 1, 2000.

evidence.supports: 1934 L-4, 1964 R-6 replacement, Tiller District history
evidence.quote: Originally the site of an L-4 constructed in 1934, it was replaced by a R-6 flattop groundhouse in 1964.

evidence.supports: 1934 L-4 built, 1964 R-6 replacement, rental program
evidence.quote: This site was first used when an L-4 cab was built in 1934. This was replaced by the present R-6 flat cab in 1964.

evidence.supports: helicopter placement in 1960s, only two remaining lookouts, rental season, access and facilities
evidence.quote: the lookout was placed on the rocky cliff via helicopter in the 1960's. Before the advent of airplane surveillance for fire detection, there were more than a dozen lookouts on the Tiller Ranger District. Today Acker Rock and Pickett Butte are the only remaining lookouts on the District.

The lookout tower is generally available for reservation from August 1st thru November 15th (depending on snow)...everything must be packed in via a moderately steep 0.4-mile hike along a forested trail to reach the lookout.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1964 built date and R-6 design matched all three sources exactly; no corrections needed.
